findings.description: Per `.claude/agents/review-docs.md`'s standing house-style rule, new prose must not introduce em/en dashes. Line 71 ("repository owner** — the person who opened...") adds an em-dash (—) in text this PR introduces. No other offending lines in this file's diff.

Step 1 of the "Turning it on" bash block is `open https://github.com/apps/claude`. `open` is macOS/BSD-specific; on Linux (including the GitHub Actions runner OS and most non-Mac dev machines) it is not a builtin and the line fails with "command not found." The repo's own positioning ("stack-agnostic... nothing assumes... layout") suggests broader OS neutrality would be preferable, e.g. dropping the `open` invocation and just presenting the bare URL to visit.

The new "Turning it on" block's step 3 (`git push origin "$(git commit-tree "$(git hash-object -t tree /dev/null)" -m 'review-metrics: init')":refs/heads/ci/review-metrics`) is technically correct and equivalent to the workflow header's existing recipe in `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` lines 7-13 (`git checkout --orphan ci/review-metrics && git rm -rf . && git commit --allow-empty ... && git push origin ci/review-metrics`) — both push a single parentless commit with the same message onto `ci/review-metrics`, and the new one-liner has the real advantage of not mutating the caller's current branch/working tree. However, the repo now documents this one-time setup action two different ways in two places with no cross-reference, which is a duplication-drift risk: if either command is revised later, the other won't be updated in step, and a reader comparing the README to the workflow header may reasonably wonder which is authoritative.

refuted_findings.description: The new README prose tells an org-repo maintainer to widen the actor gate to a team check but doesn't warn that GitHub strips write permissions from GITHUB_TOKEN on pull_request-triggered runs from forks, which could cause the Post review and persist-metrics steps to hard-fail once the gate admits fork-originated PRs.
refuted_findings.refutation: Widening the owner-only gate to "the logins (or a team check) you want to allow" naturally reads as an allowlist of trusted same-repo collaborators, not an invitation to fork-based external contributors — the inferential chain from "team check" to "fork PR" to "token downgrade" is a speculative stretch, not the common case this advice would lead someone into. More fundamentally, fork PRs on a plain `pull_request` trigger don't get repo secrets exposed either, so `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` would be unavailable and the Claude step would fail regardless of GITHUB_TOKEN permissions — the finding fixates on one failure mode while missing that the whole design already can't service fork PRs. Out of scope for a PR narrowly documenting how to turn the review on and its default owner gate.
